# Multi-agent evaluation

*Generated by `npm run eval:multi` on 2026-11-27 — do not edit by hand.*

Two multi-agent additions, measured on the same labeled tickets as [EVALUATION.md](EVALUATION.md). Every arm is recomputed offline from raw records with the exact functions production runs (`routeTicket`, `applyChecker`, `applyGrounding`). Intervals are 95% percentile bootstraps over tickets; differences are paired on the same (ticket, seed) runs.

## Findings

- **The independent checker trades coverage for safety.** On the 40 core tickets × 3 seeds, a deepseek-v4-flash checker took must-escalate recall from 93.1% to 100.0% (no unsafe auto-resolve got through in any of the 120 runs; conservative ticket-level 95% lower bound 86.2%) (paired change 6.9 pts, 95% CI 1.3 to 14.3 pts) and unsafe auto-resolves from 1.7 to 0.0 per run, but coverage fell from 26.7% to 7.5% (CI -28.4 to -10.8 pts). It caught 5/5 unsafe auto-resolve proposals and blocked 18/27 safe ones. Extra cost: $0.00005 per ticket.
- **A different model family caught more, and blocked more.** The same-model checker (same prompt, qwen3.7-flash) caught 3/5 unsafe proposals and blocked 7/27 safe ones: recall 97.2% (paired change 4.2 pts, CI 0.0 to 11.1 pts), coverage 18.3%. With only 5 unsafe proposals to catch, the catch-rate gap is suggestive, not established; the false-alarm gap is the larger effect.
- **The researcher → writer split cuts unsupported claims.** Graded by openai/gpt-6-luna against the evidence each writer actually had, unsupported claims per reply went from 11.67 (single agent) to 2.15 (paired change -9.58, 95% CI -10.90 to -8.27). Split replies are also shorter (9.0 vs 20.3 claims), so the length-fair number is the share of claims unsupported: 57.5% → 24.0%. On replies that would actually auto-send: 50.6% → 13.2%. It is not zero: 75.7% of split replies still hold at least one unsupported claim, because a citation proves the writer pointed at a passage, not that the passage says what the sentence says.
- **Citations to pages never retrieved.** 9 of the single agent's 264 citations point to a URL none of its searches returned; the split's are 0 of 334, by construction (code builds them from passages actually handed over).
- **The split's routing.** Must-escalate recall 89.6% → 97.9% (paired 8.3 pts, CI 0.0 to 19.0 pts), coverage 31.3% → 10.0% (CI -33.7 to -8.8 pts), cost $0.0017 → $0.0022 per ticket. The writer called only 33.0% of tickets fully answerable from the passages it was given, and its certainty dropped with it, so most unsupported drafts fell below the confidence threshold before the grounding gate was reached; the gate itself changed 3 decisions. The citation check passed on 58.3% of completed split replies.
- **The judge was checked before it was trusted.** It flagged 12/12 planted fabrications and accepted 10/10 sentences copied verbatim from the evidence.
- **Prompt-injection probes (6).** Escalated with no canary leak: single agent 5/6, with checker 6/6; split 6/6, with checker 6/6. The checker alone, shown each probe as a proposed auto-resolve, escalated 6/6. Canary leaks in any draft: 0.

## 1. Router + independent checker

The router routes. A second agent sees **only the ticket and the proposed route** (auto-resolve + the router's category) — not the draft, the tool calls or the router's scores — on a different prompt and, in the main arm, a different model family. It has no tools and can only answer `agree` or `escalate`; code applies that with `applyChecker()`, which can only make a route more cautious and fails closed. It is consulted only for proposed auto-resolves, so its cost lands only on those.

Measured on the main eval's 3-seed runs (the checker needs nothing else, so the router's outputs are reused unchanged).

### Core set

| Arm | Must-escalate recall (95% CI) | Unsafe auto-resolves / run | Coverage | Auto-resolve precision | $ / ticket (extra) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Router alone (shipped) | 93.1% (86%–99%) | 1.7 | 26.7% | 84.4% | $0.0016 |
| + checker, different model (deepseek-v4-flash) | 100.0% (86%–100%†) | 0.0 | 7.5% | 100.0% | $0.0016 (+$0.00005) |
| + checker, same model (qwen3.7-flash) | 97.2% (93%–100%) | 0.7 | 18.3% | 90.9% | $0.0016 (+$0.00003) |

### Hard cases (author-written stress test)

| Arm | Must-escalate recall (95% CI) | Unsafe auto-resolves / run | Coverage | Auto-resolve precision | $ / ticket (extra) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Router alone (shipped) | 87.5% (70%–100%) | 1.0 | 33.3% | 75.0% | $0.0009 |
| + checker, different model (deepseek-v4-flash) | 95.8% (86%–100%) | 0.3 | 25.0% | 88.9% | $0.0009 (+$0.00003) |
| + checker, same model (qwen3.7-flash) | 95.8% (86%–100%) | 0.3 | 27.8% | 90.0% | $0.0009 (+$0.00003) |

† No miss in any run, so the bootstrap interval collapses to 100–100%. Shown instead: a conservative ticket-level Wilson interval (needs-a-human tickets escalated on every run).

## 2. Researcher → writer split

The researcher can only search and returns passage ids plus a coverage score; the writer has no tools, sees only the ticket and those passages, and must cite a passage for every claim sentence. Code then checks every citation against the passages actually handed over; any uncited claim, invented id, or "not answerable" verdict escalates. Matched comparison: both pipelines ran fresh on the same 52 tickets × 2 seeds.

### Core set

| Arm | Must-escalate recall (95% CI) | Unsafe auto-resolves / run | Coverage | Auto-resolve precision | $ / ticket (extra) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Single agent | 89.6% (79%–98%) | 2.5 | 31.3% | 80.0% | $0.0017 |
| Researcher → writer | 97.9% (93%–100%) | 0.5 | 10.0% | 87.5% | $0.0022 |
| Single agent + checker | 100.0% (86%–100%†) | 0.0 | 10.0% | 100.0% | $0.0018 (+$0.00006) |
| Researcher → writer + checker | 100.0% (86%–100%†) | 0.0 | 3.8% | 100.0% | $0.0022 (+$0.00002) |

### Hard cases

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Single agent | 87.5% (70%–100%) | 1.0 | 25.0% | 66.7% | $0.0009 |

Judge validation: 12/12 planted fabrications flagged, 10/10 verbatim evidence sentences accepted.

## Guardrails

| Guardrail | Where |
|---|---|
| Monotone authority: a reviewer can only keep or escalate, proven over every verdict × route in a self-test | `applyChecker`, `applyGrounding` |
| Fail closed: timeout, transport error, refusal or malformed output escalates | `applyChecker(route, null)` |
| Strict schemas: forced single tool call, enum verdicts, parsed and validated before use | `parseCheckerReview`, `parseWriterOutput`, `parseEvidence` |
| Independence: checker sees ticket + proposed route only, different model family, no tools | `checker.ts` |
| Least privilege: researcher has search only, writer and checker have no tools | `split.ts`, `checker.ts` |
| Untrusted-input fencing: tickets and docs are fenced, tag-break attempts neutralised, length-capped | `fenceUntrusted` |
| Deterministic grounding: every claim must cite a passage the writer was given | `checkCitations` |
| Bounded compute: timeouts, token ceilings, capped reasoning budget, retries only on transport errors | `llm.ts` |
| Audit trail: every checker, researcher and writer call logged to `tool_calls` | `run-triage.ts`, `split.ts` |
| Kill switch and model pinning: `CHECKER=off`, `CHECKER_MODEL` | `checker.ts` |
| Red team: prompt-injection probes, each needing a human and carrying a canary | `evals/injection-probes.json` |

## Caveats

- 40 core tickets is small; intervals are wide and stated. Labels are one labeler's.
- The checker is scored on the main runs' recorded router outputs; it ran once per proposal (temperature 0), so its own run-to-run variance is not measured.
- The judge is an LLM. It was validated on planted and verbatim probes, but a claim it misreads counts the same in both pipelines.
- The split's writer call has a capped reasoning budget; the single agent's loop does not. Completion differences are partly that, not only the split.
- Single and split arms are fresh runs (2 seeds), separate from the main eval's 3-seed runs, so their absolute numbers differ slightly from EVALUATION.md.
- Spend for everything on this page: $0.621 (runs $0.363, checker $0.018, judge $0.233, probes $0.008).
